blocks.text: The lattice energy of a compound cannot be determined by a single direct experiment, but it can be calculated from several experimental data using an energy cycle called the Born-Haber cycle, an application of Hess's law.

blocks.alt: Triangle of three light-blue boxes: Na(s) + 1/2 Cl2(g) (top left), Na+Cl-(s) (top right) and Na+(g) + Cl-(g) (bottom). Arrow top left to top right: delta H(o)f. Arrow from the elements down to the gaseous ions: delta Hx. Arrow from the gaseous ions up to Na+Cl-(s): delta H(o)latt.
blocks.caption: Figure 6.8: Enthalpy cycle of sodium chloride (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 6.8).

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The printed Figure 6.8 gives the product as Na+Cl-(g) and draws the lattice-energy arrow from the solid to the gaseous ions. The product is solid NaCl, Na+Cl-(s), and the lattice energy is released from the gaseous ions to the solid, as drawn above.

For sodium chloride the elements Na(s) + 1/2 Cl2(g) form the solid NaCl directly (delta Hf, the standard enthalpy of formation, measured conveniently in a calorimeter) or go through the gaseous ions Na+(g) + Cl-(g): delta Hx is the total energy involved in changing sodium and chlorine from their standard states to gaseous ions, and the gaseous ions then form the solid (delta Hlatt). By Hess's law delta Hx + delta Hlatt = delta Hf.
The energy triangle extended to show the stages of delta Hx is the complete Born-Haber cycle.

blocks.alt: Born-Haber ladder, not to scale. From the reactants level Na(s) + 1/2 Cl2(g): up by delta Hat of Na = +108 kJ mol-1 to Na(g) + 1/2 Cl2(g); up by delta Hi of Na = +496 kJ mol-1 to Na+(g) + e- + 1/2 Cl2(g); up by delta Hat of Cl2 = +121 kJ mol-1 to Na+(g) + e- + Cl(g); down by delta Hea of Cl = -349 kJ mol-1 to Na+(g) + Cl-(g); a thick arrow down, delta Hlatt = ? (lattice energy of NaCl), to the final product Na+Cl-(s). From the reactants an arrow goes down to Na+Cl-(s): delta Hf = -411.
blocks.caption: Figure 6.9: Born Haber cycle of sodium chloride (not according to scale) (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 6.9).

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The printed Figure 6.9 writes 'Na+(g) + 1/2 Cl2' where Na(g) + 1/2 Cl2(g) is meant, and 'Cl2(g)' at the top where Cl(g) is meant; both are drawn correctly above.

blocks.caption: Born-Haber cycle of NaCl (Figure 6.9), kJ per mol
rows: Lattice energy = delta Hf - delta Hx

blocks.text: Sample Problem 6.9: the heat of formation of sodium fluoride, which crystallizes in the sodium chloride lattice, from its cycle. The heat of atomization of Na(s) is 109, half the bond energy of F2 is 79, the ionization energy of sodium is 494, the electron affinity of fluorine is -328 and the lattice energy is -939 kJ per mol: delta Hf = -939 + 109 + 494 + 79 - 328 = -585 kJ per mol.
